findings.text: The rseq system call dispatches by flags and current registration state. An unregister request uses the unregister path. Any unsupported flag bit causes rejection. When the caller already holds a registration the request uses the reregister path which never reinstalls. Otherwise length and alignment are validated before registration proceeds.
The slice yield system call reports whether the current task had latched a revoked grant observation and then clears that latch, so repeated calls stay idle until another revocation occurs.

Pending slice work at system call entry guarantees timer cancellation, a reschedule request unless already preempted, revocation of the grant in both kernel and user state, and latching of a yield observation only for the cooperative yield call, with debug builds validating user control consistency.
The statistics thread wakes periodically to emit aggregated counters, absorbs global shutdown parks, and exits only after the global stop condition and the thread stop request are both observable.

A globally visible helper arms the per CPU slice timer for the current task with an absolute deadline while asserting masked interrupts, recording task identity for later validation and requesting immediate rescheduling when the deadline already passed.

A globally visible control helper implements query and update of per task slice enable state, rejecting unknown operations, spare argument bits, unsupported kernels, missing registration and legacy version registrations, and updating user flags together with task state.

The torture layer exposes helpers to emit hotplug statistics, to park during global shutdown, to query the stop indicator from normal and interrupt contexts, to block until thread exit is requested, and to draw pseudo random values.

The slice subsystem exposes a duration tunable marked for mostly read access, a static branch key governing the feature, and boot helpers that honor a boolean command line switch and install per CPU timer callbacks.
Per CPU slice state pairs a high resolution timer with an opaque identity cookie used to confirm the arming task is still running when the timer fires, with one instance resident on each CPU.

Per thread torture statistics bundle a thread reference and CPU number with separate tallies for reschedule calls and for single, single remote, many and broadcast call variants, distinguishing waiting use and offloaded delivery where applicable.
A selector entry holds a cumulative weight threshold with a primitive identifier and a wait marker, kept in a fixed capacity table with a used length and a running total weight.
A call check descriptor carries inbound and outbound markers with a target CPU, wait and remote markers, a completion object for synchronous remote use, and an intrusive list node for freelist reuse.
Original restartable sequence area length is 32 bytes.
Only the slice extension default on flag is accepted during registration and all other flag bits are rejected.
Slice extension duration lower bound corresponds to five microseconds and upper bound to fifty microseconds, with the current tunable starting at the lower bound.
Torture primitive identifiers are reschedule zero, single one, single remote two, many three and broadcast four, with table capacity eight to cover waiting and non waiting variants of each.

A length below the original size is invalid. A length equal to the original size requires original size alignment. A larger length requires allocator alignment and must extend through the end marker of the extended layout.

Registration establishes a matched pair of user and task state where user critical section state is null, flags reflect slice availability and enablement, identity fields hold reset values, and task state records pointer length signature plus versioned presence with a forced refresh before user mode resume.

Unregistration succeeds only with flag bits inside the unregister mask, a supplied pointer matching a non null current registration, equal lengths, and equal signatures, where signature mismatch yields permission failure and other mismatches yield invalid argument.

A repeat registration with identical pointer length and signature reports busy without mutating state, while pointer or length divergence yields invalid argument and signature divergence yields permission failure.

Enable query rejects spare arguments and reports current enablement, while enable update requires feature support with an existing version two registration and consistent user flag state before flipping user and task enablement together.

The duration control accepts only decimal input within the configured minimum and maximum inclusive, rejecting parse failures and out of range values and otherwise publishing the new duration while reporting full consumption.
The duration file presents a single value view where open read seek and release behavior comes from single and sequential helpers and writes go through the range checked parser.
Boot option parsing honors only boolean values and disables the feature key when false, while early setup installs a monotonic relative pinned timer callback on every possible CPU.
Selector insertion ignores zero weight entries and refuses table overflow, scaled percentage accounting overflow, and primitive identifiers beyond the known name table.
Each primitive identifier maps to a readable operation name used when logging the configured selection distribution.

The torture callback always accounts one per CPU invocation, treats missing inbound marking as an ordering error, applies randomized short or configured long delays, then either completes synchronous remote waiters with an outbound mark or recycles the descriptor for asynchronous use.
The single target variant checks execution happens on the expected CPU and counts placement mismatches as errors before delegating to the shared handler.

Periodic reporting sums per CPU invocation counts with per thread operation tallies across all threads and prefixes the line with an alert marker whenever placement, ordering or allocation error counters are active outside sanitizer builds.
Hotplug success attempt minima maxima and sum statistics are emitted only when CPU hotplug support is configured.
The torture random source reseeds from time and CPU after a fixed number of draws and otherwise advances by multiply add before returning a byte swapped value.
Idle check descriptors wait on per CPU pools indexed by current CPU modulo thread count, with a per CPU drain that unlinks every entry and releases each one.
Torture logging uses a fixed module tag with a spaced flag prefix and provides conditional verbose and unconditional error output variants.
Shutdown testing and torture type selection are build or parameter controlled, with distinct build variants for disabled versus enabled shutdown behavior.
Global torture state comprises a per thread statistics array with a statistics thread reference plus a per CPU invocation counter and per CPU free pools.
Progress and health use atomic tallies for started threads and for placement, inbound ordering, outbound ordering and allocation errors, alongside a done flag and a mutable alert prefix.

A task moves from unregistered to registered upon successful validation and initialization, stays registered across repeat attempts that never mutate state, and returns to unregistered only through a fully validated unregister that resets identity and clears task state.

Slice state moves from disabled to enabled by registration flags or control update, to granted with an armed timer, then to revoked on system call entry or expiry, with a latched yield observation persisting until consumed by the yield call.
Torture threads cycle between periodic work and shutdown parking while the global indicator remains in run state, then drain through a stopping handshake until the thread stop request is observable.

Selection state is built by accumulating total weight with per entry cumulative thresholds, reported as percent shares with three decimal places, and sampled by drawing within total weight inclusive and returning the first covering entry.

Slice entry work disables preemption to stabilize the per CPU timer reference and to keep reschedule marking correct on fully preemptible kernels, adding an explicit reschedule check for cooperative models.
Reschedule requests from slice context mask interrupts around the update to prevent an interrupt level schedule from clearing task state between the task and preemption markings.

Timer and cookie state rely on CPU locality with disabled preemption or disabled interrupts instead of a spinlock, using identity comparison to tolerate scheduling away without cancellation and a best effort local cancel.

User memory access failures during registration, grant revocation, control validation or enable updates produce fault status or forced segmentation signals without leaving partially updated kernel state.

A deadline that passed before user mode return still forces rescheduling even without an armed timer, and a grant already revoked by a kernel race is ignored at system call entry to avoid duplicate accounting.
Shared delivery to multiple receivers reuses one descriptor with outbound state cleared per delivery, counting missing inbound state separately from CPU placement errors.
